S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a full incident report within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when the incident presents a credible safety risk, and promptly provide safety instructions and material updates.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% triggers prompt regulator notification, independent confirmatory testing, and a corrective-action plan on a regulator-set timeline; it is not, by itself, an automatic sales ban. Manufacturers must provide per-model results, sample sizes, and methods to the regulator and make them available to customers who purchase or own that model; public publication is not required.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support this function within 6 years of adoption, prioritizing units with elevated risk and providing a documented retrofit schedule.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The suppression system must be appropriate to the battery chemistry and installation, independently validated, and maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model's thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 per 100,000 installed units during any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide supporting data and methodology. A confirmed exceedance does not, by itself, automatically trigger a recall. The regulator must order a recall and customer notification, with a remedy and safety instructions, when its review finds the model presents an unacceptable safety risk.

document.section_notes: The final text keeps the 5% test benchmark but removes any automatic sales stop, and it leaves per-model results with regulators and purchasers rather than the public. S5 requires no mandatory recall at the 8 per 100,000 threshold; the trigger only prompts verification, corrective action, and regulator-ordered recall on risk findings, so the permanent_trigger_per_100k field is recorded as null. The 6-year retrofit (S3) and 36-month suppression deadline (S4) sit within the acceptable ranges, and S1 is the strongest section, with 24-hour reporting of all thermal incidents.
